title: Behavioral fingerprinting harness for multiplexed streaming + tool-call regressions
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Build a deterministic, repeatable harness that computes a compact behavioral fingerprint for a request/response interaction across streaming transports, multiplexed client sessions, and tool/function-call sequences. This harness will be the core of a new regression gate: instead of only exact token diffs we compute a stability score that tolerates legitimate non-determinism (timestamps, IDs) while surfacing semantic regressions and tool-call reordering bugs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Fingerprint generator produces compact, human-readable hash + signature for a set of golden interactions. 2) CI job fails when score delta > 0.08 against golden baseline for a route. 3) Replayer can deterministically reproduce the interaction using recorded events and stubbed tools. 4) Test matrix covers: single-stream, multiplexed sessions (N=10), function-call nesting, early stream cancellations, and KV cache warm/cold scenarios.
test_plan:
- Create a corpus of 120 golden interactions (text + streaming chunks + tool call traces + structured outputs).
- Implement normalization rules: strip monotonic IDs, normalize timestamps to window, canonicalize whitespace and JSON key order.
- Implement fingerprint algorithm: sequence-aware rolling hash + semantic token grouping + tool-call graph hash.
- Build deterministic replayer that can run in unit CI with stubbed tool endpoints.
- Add CI matrix: linux x64, linux-airgapped (simulated), and dedicated-capacity smoke lane.
- Add flaky-tolerance experiments to set threshold per-route via metadata.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Ava M: Initial spike completed. Prototype normalizer handles ISO timestamps and UUID removal. Early hashing approach: xxh3 + event-sequence prefixing.
2026-02-26 - Ravi S: Reviewed normalization rules with @Lena O'Connor. Agreed to preserve relative ordering of tool calls and collapse identical contiguous tokens to reduce noise.

2026-03-02 - Lena O'Connor: Design feedback: ensure structured-output canonicalization keeps schema forward-compatible (use stable path hashing). Added acceptance criterion for tool-call graph hash stability.

2026-03-05 - Ravi S: Implemented replayer and added 30 golden interactions to ci/regress/goldens. Observed two failures: (a) streaming chunk boundary shifts causing false positives, (b) kv-cache cold start causing message duplication. Added normalization to merge adjacent short chunks and dedupe cache-refetched tokens.

2026-03-08 - QA: Flaky experiment ran 2000 iterations; baseline threshold of 0.08 drops false positives to <0.5% while catching deliberate semantic changes in the corpus. Need a short RFC to finalize thresholds per-route.
2026-03-10 - Ravi S: Opened PRs for runtime + ci-helpers. Coordinating with infra to expose stubbed tool endpoints in the dedicated smoke lane (ENG-61234 dependency).
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive normalization reduces noise but risks masking subtle regressions (e.g., schema changes that only modify non-essential fields). To mitigate this, we maintain two-level fingerprints: 'surface' (permissive) and 'strict' (no normalization). CI will gate on a combination: surface must be stable; strict used for targeted high-sensitivity routes.
next_steps:
- Finalize normalization RFC (owners: Ravi, Lena) by 2026-03-12.
- Merge PRs and enable ci/regress/fingerprint-smoke as a required check on runtime releases.
- Expand golden corpus to 120 interactions and add per-route thresholds to the goldens manifest.
- Add docs for teams to record new golden interactions and mark stable routes in Confluence.
long_term: Integrate fingerprint scoring into Console's rollout UI so rollouts can show semantic delta heatmaps and auto-block if high-impact regressions are detected. Consider ML-based clustering of deltas to prioritize human review.
